scope: Proposition 7.1 (Area envelope and regular patches) of the manuscript “A Charged Reduction of the Spacetime Penrose Inequality in Spatial Dimensions at Least Four” (preprints/A-Charged-Reduction-of-the-Spacetime-Penrose-Inequality-in-Spatial-Dimensions-at-Least-Four-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3e5e445d305051a1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 53. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The least perimeter of filled competitors equals the full smooth-cut infimum a. The family F∗ of minimizing filled sets, considered modulo null sets, is compact in local L1, and all its members are supported in a common compact set. Their exterior end components have the full-boundary convention of Definition 2.3. Each minimizing frontier is smooth and minimal at its free regular points. Its possible singular set has Hausdorff dimension at most n − 8. All contact points with S are regular of class C1,γ for some γ > 0, and their graph representations belong to W2,p for every finite p. At an interior regular point of one frontier, any other minimizing frontier through the point coincides with it locally. On a smaller neighborhood the minimizing frontiers that meet that neighborhood are disjoint single graphs, with uniform smooth interior estimates. For a differentiable metric path with g′ 0 = h, the right derivative of its enclosing-area infimum is a′ +(h) = min F∈F∗ a′ F (h), a′ F (h) = 1 2 ∫ ∂∗F trT∂∗F h dAg. (7.4) Here and below ∂∗F is used for integration, while “frontier” means the support of its perimeter measure.
